question: Can scheduled Chat authenticate an external proof-carrying manifest/attestation without running a cryptographic verifier or relying on a quota-bearing hosted verification service?

public_evidence.source: GitHub REST API endpoints for Git commits
public_evidence.finding: Git commit responses expose a verification object with verified:boolean, reason, signature, signed payload and verified_at; reason=valid means GitHub considers the commit signature verified.

Blob verification requires the artifact, verification bundle and signer identity, and the documented path invokes cosign verify-blob; Cosign performs certificate, artifact-signature and transparency-log checks.
The official workflow says to install Cosign and execute cosign verify/verify-blob. Raw signature/bundle presence is therefore not itself verified evidence on this Chat surface.

connector_capability_discovery.note: The exposed create_commit action accepts repository, message, tree and parent(s), but no signature. Contents writes in this invocation produced an unsigned commit.

candidate_matrix.candidate: Trust own role-local repository path/blob identity under the already-authorized repository boundary
candidate_matrix.boundary: Authenticates repository state/identity because repository itself is an allowed authority/transport; does not authenticate arbitrary external authors.

candidate_matrix.quota_fragility: no monthly quota identified for read-side verification metadata
candidate_matrix.boundary: Current connector-created commits are unsigned and connector exposes no signing parameter/action, so this cannot presently authenticate newly produced own manifests without an independently available signer.
Official verification invokes Cosign and multiple cryptographic checks; simply parsing a bundle is not verification.

candidate_matrix.candidate: Treat signature/attestation text as trusted because it is present
candidate_matrix.boundary: Presence of bytes/claims cannot establish authenticity.

result.positive_narrow_result: Provider-reported verification metadata can be consumed without local cryptographic execution if an already-signed commit exists and its verification object is valid; this was not demonstrated for a current role-produced artifact because the live role-local commit was unsigned.
result.effect_on_r150: Keep r150 proof-carrying manifest authority strictly role-local/repository-authorized. Do not upgrade it to arbitrary external signed-manifest support.
result.residual_dependency_description: For newly authored external-authentic manifests, a signer plus actual signature verifier (or a provider-verification path over an already-signed object) is still required.
result.finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota_dependen: Not used in this test; raw Sigstore route rejected before quota analysis because it needs cryptographic execution not exposed as a Chat-native verifier.

frontier: Search for repository-native signed tag/release/commit objects that are already externally signed and whose provider verification status is exposed; use only verification metadata, never commit message semantics.
Test whether an already-present signed public artifact can be admitted as read-only evidence with zero optional quota, while keeping fresh signing unresolved.
Continue bounded unsigned role-local proof manifests under repository authority for outcomes that do not require external authorship.
